probe.note: Five neutral probe solves (weighted sum, no floors) of the actual design problem; values are achieved, feasible designs. Ranges are indicative, not exhaustive.

justification.normalisation: Ranges span the probe-achieved values, with the lower ends set at or just below the worst probe (runtime 45.2 h, siren 2.1 h, voice 74.6, L5 0.073) and the upper ends just above the best probe (62.3 h, 3.14 h, 77.7, 0.267), so no objective's scale is inflated or shrunk.
justification.scalarisation: The probes show a real conflict (L5 0.267 costs runtime 45 h, runtime 62 h costs L5 0.07), so achievement (Tchebycheff) is used to reach balanced Pareto points that a weighted sum could miss.
justification.aspiration: Runtime 60 h is the marketing target and is within the probe range. Siren 3.1 h and voice 77 are just below the best probe values (3.141 and 77.7). L5 0.14 sits between the equal-weight probe (0.174) and the siren/runtime probes (0.07-0.09) because siren >= 3 h and runtime ~60 h together limit L5.
justification.objective_floors: Siren endurance >= 3 h is a stated program requirement, and the siren probe reached 3.141 h feasibly, so a 3.0 h floor is attainable. Runtime (~60 h) and L5 are goals, and voice is described only as 'good', so they get no floors.
justification.weights: Runtime has the highest weight as the headline marketing goal. Siren and L5 are weighted equally, with L5 being the objective most compressed by the siren floor. Voice has the lowest weight because its probe range is narrow (74.6-77.7) and every probe already gives acceptable SII.
